_comment: English hero backgrounds: OCR of the English board backs, corrected by hand. Typical OCR errors fixed: b/h (bim, bead, bowever), I/T (Ihe, Ihere), Ores/Orcs, Il/II, dropped apostrophes; the 'Suggested start' block that was glued to three texts is removed; paragraph breaks follow the printed layout (the Russian backs keep the same paragraphs).

hero-aragorn.background_en:
The Dunedain of the North were nearly destroyed. Although their number is few, they continue to watch and guard the lands that were once their kingdom. At their head is their Chieftain, Aragorn, descendant of Isildur, a Man destined for greatness.
The prophecies and lineage serve him little in this time, however. Bloodlines cannot stop a foe's blade, and songs of future glory do not feed one's people. Though years of peace and prosperity may come, these are no such years. Now is a time of trials, hardship, and survival. New dangers threaten the North in ever greater number, and darker years are yet to come.

hero-arwen.background_en:
Arwen Undomiel, face as fair as that of Luthien, fate as grand as that of Beren, carries the legacy of her ancestors forward. She, like her father Elrond before her, possesses the talent to see the threads of futures woven together. She holds both past and future like clear water cupped in her hands. Her words carry great wisdom for those who listen to her advice.
However, the future is not yet set in stone, and seeking to guide it toward the light will lead Arwen away from her people and out of her forest. The dangers she goes to confront are many, but wherever she goes she will be the Evenstar of the Elves, bringing light and wisdom to all.

hero-balin.background_en:
On his many journeys through the long years, Balin has never met a challenge that dissuaded him for long. The darker the path, the more treasures that might lay hidden from view, only waiting for the brave and the clever to uncover them. After Balin successfully reclaimed Erebor with Thorin's company, the Dwarves thrived. But Balin hungered for new adventures, and new discoveries.
Now, Balin is ready to make another journey, perhaps even into the darkened halls of Khazad-dum that were abandoned so long ago. The lost treasures there tempt him to delve deeper than he ever has before, and he yearns to see a king sit upon the throne under the Misty Mountains again.

hero-beorn.background_en:
There are none alive who truly know how old Beorn is, and those who would gain such knowledge are hard-pressed to track him down in his isolation, let alone entice him to share more than a few curt words. But after helping Bilbo and the Dwarves reclaim Erebor, Beorn has found aiding the wider world to be more rewarding than he once thought.
Bees and hounds are Beorn's trusted companions more than soldiers and historians. But throughout his long centuries of life, Beorn has seen the darkness grow stronger, consuming man and beast alike. His answer to the growing danger is simple: axe and tooth and claw.

hero-the-great-bear.background_en:
The Great Bear is Beorn's alternate form. Beorn is The Great Bear's alternate form.
You cannot start a campaign or adventure as this hero. During setup, set this hero card aside with The Great Bear figure and the mandated equipment listed below. When a skill card instructs a hero to “change,” they replace their hero card, figure, and all of their equipped items with the alternate form hero card, figure, and items.
(See Changing Form on page 4 of the Spreading War rulebook.)

hero-beravor.background_en:
As a Ranger of the North, Beravor knows the hidden roads of Middle-earth, through barren hills, tangled wood, and unquieted ruins. These secret paths are her frequent course, gifting both safety and speed through otherwise perilous lands.
Nothing can cause this Ranger to stray but the call for aid from the imperiled, whether ally or stranger—and no matter the cause, no matter the danger, she is ready for the fight. In a time when the dark expanse between the lands of the Free Peoples is ever growing, the swiftness, knowledge, and valour of Beravor are coveted qualities that many will soon require.

hero-bilbo.background_en:
Not many years ago, Bilbo travelled east from the Shire and it changed him forever. He is not entirely different, still enjoying warm food, polite company, uninterrupted rest, and holes in the ground that contain neither Goblin nor Dragon—nor riddling, murderous creatures, for that matter.
At his core, however, something has altered. He is now a wanderer, burglar, warrior, and, though he dare not tell his neighbours, adventurer. He has sprung into action and fled for his life. He has sheathed a bloodied blade, flown with Eagles, and stood atop the wealth of kingdoms. That Tookish part, now awoken, does not easily lay back to rest. It may be time for another adventure.

hero-boromir.background_en:
Boromir, eldest son of the twenty-sixth Steward of Gondor, Denethor II, loves his land with the burning ferocity of dragon-fire. As a young and rising star of Gondor's army, he has gained glory and respect on the battlefield. As a son and a brother, he would do anything to aid his family.
But Gondor faces dark times ahead, and the people look for more than just a soldier in him. He must become a hero who can save not only Gondor, but all of Middle-earth, and prove that there is still hope and valour in the line of Mardil the Steadfast, who swore the first Steward's oath to keep Gondor safe until the King returned.

hero-calaminth-took.background_en:
Many a weary traveller on the road has been comforted and cheered at the end of the day by the sight of a small cookfire and a friendly face ready to share a story. But very few Hobbits would prefer a dusty campfire to a proper stone hearth. Calaminth Took is the exception.
She has wandered far from the Shire, through Bree, and into the wild lands beyond in search of the kinds of legends told by firelight. Everywhere she goes, she brings the comforts that Hobbits hold dear, and all who share her fire count themselves lucky. But for any who see only a soft wanderer in her guise, a warning: a Took can wield a ladle or a mace with equal ferocity.

hero-dis.background_en:
Dis has seen the world grow darker. The hope in travellers' eyes grows dim and fearful as enemies stalk the roads. Her own brother, Thorin Oakenshield, and her two sons, Fili and Kili, were all slain recapturing Erebor. As the last surviving member of her family, and one of the greatest smiths of the mountains, Dis cannot justify letting others do the much-needed work any longer.
It is time for her to take the best of her craft and all of her years of cunning and bring them to bear against the foes of Middle-earth. Let those who stand against her beware: a Dwarf does not rest until the battlefield is empty.

hero-dwalin.background_en:
After residing in Erebor and seeing the Dwarves prosper, Dwalin feels called to venture into the wider world for one more great adventure. He knows that the gathered wisdom of many kingdoms could bring even more wealth and progress for the Dwarves of the Lonely Mountain.
Though, perhaps it is the ancient anger that all Dwarves hold in their hearts that drives Dwalin to leave his mountain home in favor of a battlefield of Orcs. The years have taken their toll on Dwalin's combat prowess, but his courage in battle has not diminished with time. Surely, whether he pursues the thrill of war or greater wisdom, Dwalin will prove a valuable ally in any quest.

hero-eleanor.background_en:
As a noblewoman of Gondor, Eleanor is familiar with the endless work of defending settled lands from the enemy. As soon as she came of age, Eleanor took to the roads, carrying messages between remote villages in the mountains. Every year, it seems, more Orcs threaten the border and more brave soldiers fall to the foe's cursed weapons, never to rise again.
But Gondor is not the only land threatened by growing evil, and Eleanor is a woman ready to see the wider world. She hopes to return someday to Gondor, her beloved land between the mountains and the sea, with better ways to protect her people from the enemy.

hero-elena.background_en:
Born in the great port city of Mithlond, Elena has watched for years as hosts of her kin take to the sea, retreating toward the Undying Lands. Even the population of her own city begins to dwindle, with Elves of every age and vocation, save for the shipwrights, disappearing westward.
Nothing remains for her in these forsaken lands but the beauty of this fading. As the blazing glory of the setting sun or the climactic splendor of a final chorus, so is the passing of the Elves. Having gathered the stories and songs of those who fled west, Elena now sets out to seek the tales of those who remain and perhaps, if she is fortunate, partake in one of her own.

hero-freahild.background_en:
The Shieldmaidens of Rohan are sung about in countless legends, but very few of their lineage remain in this age. Freahild is one of their number, trained as a youth to defend Rohan from all the enemies who seek to threaten its borders. Perhaps as famous as the Shieldmaidens, the fine horses of Rohan are bred to be swift and strong and agile. Freahild has trusted Snowbright, one of the finest mounts Rohan has to offer, to carry her safely across torn battlefields and storm-swept plains for years. Freahild treasures that loyal companionship more highly than Dragon's gold.
Even in the chaos of war, Snowbright and Freahild are home as long as they have each other.

hero-gandalf.background_en:
Gandalf is known by many names. Some know him only as the Grey Pilgrim, while others call him Stormcrow, or Greyhame. Though he looks old and stooped, his gaze can unsettle those who are not used to the wise wizard, giving them the sense that he knows more than he ought, and sees things they might prefer to hide.
Gandalf has powers at his command that are beyond what mortals can wield, for he is of the Istari. As a member of the White Council, Gandalf is chiefly concerned with keeping the forces of corruption and shadow at bay. He knows what could come to pass if the Council falters.

hero-gimli.background_en:
Gimli, son of Gloin, descendant of Durin the Deathless, long burned for adventure beyond his exile-home in Ered Luin. When Gloin joined a company traveling east to reclaim the forfeited Kingdom under the Mountain, Gimli could not join their number. Now, however, being of a respectable age, Gimli is ready to release his ferocity and expertise upon his foes.
Like any Dwarf, a passion churns within to deliver retribution on the vile Orcs that dwell in the darkness beneath the earth. One need not travel below to find them now, however, and so Gimli waits, restless, for the first call for deliverance from, or war against, the rising darkness.

hero-legolas.background_en:
Where many Elves of Mirkwood are skilled, Legolas excels: with bow and blade, perceiving what others cannot and moving without impediment or trace. Nevertheless, as son to the king of the Woodland Realm, much of Legolas' life is overshadowed by the grandeur of his father, even as the kingdom shrinks before the darkness in the South.
Where once the borders of Mirkwood were revered, now Orcs, Dwarves, and even stranger folk called Hobbits travel. The world is in motion, fueled by a spreading darkness. Whether at home or abroad, Legolas stands ready to lend his superior talent and skill in the fight against the rising evil.

hero-renerien.background_en:
“Being clever is often better than being mighty” is a piece of advice oft repeated by Cirdan, the shipwright of the Elves. In his daughter Renerien, those words have proven to be a great truth. Renerien is as inventive as any shipwright, but she is not content to stay at port.
She has seen many of her kin travel to the West, and knows that she has much she wants to accomplish before taking that journey herself. Joy lights her eyes, even when the shadow of cruelty and war darken the lands through which she travels, because she knows that there are often solutions hidden in the most tangled of wrecks for those brave and clever enough to find them.
